title.zh: 卷三十二 列傳第二 后妃下
title.en: Volume 32 Biographies 2: Empresses and Consorts Part Two
title.raw: 卷三十二 列傳第二 后妃下 Volume 32 Biographies 2: Empresses and Consorts Part Two

sentences.zh: 元敬虞皇后

translations.literal: Empress Yu, posthumous epithet Yuanjing (“Respectful”).
translations.idiomatic: Empress Yu the Respectful

sentences.zh: 元敬虞皇后諱孟母，濟陽外黃人也。

translations.literal: The Yuanjing Empress Yu’s taboo name was Mengmu; she was a native of Waihuang in Jiyang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Yu the Respectful, whose personal name was Mengmu, came from Waihuang in Jiyang.

sentences.zh: 父豫，見《外戚傳》。

translations.literal: Her father was Yu; see the “Biographies of the Consort Families.”
translations.idiomatic: Her father was Yu Yu; his life is recorded under the consort kin.

sentences.zh: 帝為琅邪王，納后為妃，無子。

translations.literal: When the Emperor was Prince of Langya, he took her as consort; she bore no sons.
translations.idiomatic: While he was still Prince of Langya, he married her as his consort, and she had no children.

sentences.zh: 永嘉六年薨，時年三十五。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of the Yongjia era she died; she was thirty-five sui.
translations.idiomatic: She died in 312, at the age of thirty-five.

sentences.zh: 帝為晉王，追尊為王后。

translations.literal: When he became Prince of Jin, he posthumously honored her as queen consort.
translations.idiomatic: Once he was invested as Prince of Jin, he posthumously raised her to the rank of queen consort.

sentences.zh: 有司奏王后應別立廟。

translations.literal: The responsible officials memorialized that the queen consort ought to have a separate ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: Officials proposed that she receive a shrine of her own, apart from the main imperial cult.

sentences.zh: 令曰：「今宗廟未成，不宜更興作，便修飾陵上屋以為廟。

translations.literal: An order said: “The dynastic temple is not yet complete; it is not fitting to launch further construction; instead, refurbish the buildings atop her tumulus and use them as the temple.”
translations.idiomatic: He issued an order: “The imperial ancestral temple is still unfinished, so we should not start another major project; renovate the structures on her mound and let that serve as her shrine.”

sentences.zh: 」太興三年，冊曰：「皇帝咨前琅邪王妃虞氏：朕祗順昊天成命，用陟帝位。

translations.literal: ” In the third year of the Taixing era, the investiture text read: “The Emperor addresses the former Princess of Langya, Lady Yu: I have reverently complied with August Heaven’s completed Mandate and thereby ascended the imperial throne.”
translations.idiomatic: ” In 320, the formal patent ran: “The Emperor speaks to Lady Yu, once consort to the Prince of Langya: I have bowed to Heaven’s Mandate and taken the throne.”

sentences.zh: 悼妃夙徂，徽音潛翳，御于家邦，靡所儀刑，陰教有虧，用傷于懷。

translations.literal: The lamented consort died early; her fine repute lies hidden; in ruling the household and state there is none by whom to take pattern; inner-chamber instruction suffers lack—thereby my breast is wounded.
translations.idiomatic: My consort was taken too soon; her virtuous memory has faded; within the palace and across the realm there is no one left to embody her example, and the teaching proper to the inner quarters stands impaired—this grieves me deeply.

sentences.zh: 追號制諡，先王之典。

translations.literal: Conferring a posthumous title and crafting an epithet are precedents of the former kings.
translations.idiomatic: Bestowing a posthumous name and style is what the sages of old established as right.

sentences.zh: 今遣使持節兼太尉萬勝奉冊贈皇后璽綬，祀以太牢。

translations.literal: Now I dispatch bearer of credentials concurrently Grand Commandant Wan Sheng to present the patent and confer the empress’s seal-cords, sacrificing with a grand ox.
translations.idiomatic: I therefore send Wan Sheng, credential-bearing envoy and concurrent Grand Commandant, to deliver the patent and the empress’s seals and ribbons, with sacrifice of the highest grade.

sentences.zh: 魂而有靈，嘉茲寵榮。

translations.literal: If your soul has awareness, rejoice in this favor and glory.
translations.idiomatic: Should your spirit endure, take comfort in this honor we pay you.

sentences.zh: 」乃祔於太廟，葬建平陵。

translations.literal: ” Thereupon she received joint worship in the Grand Temple and was buried at Jianping Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: She was then enshrined with the imperial ancestors and laid to rest at Jianping Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 太寧中，明帝追懷母養之恩，贈豫妻王氏為䢵陽縣君，從母散騎常侍新野王罕妻為平陽鄉君。

translations.literal: During the Taining era, Emperor Ming, recollecting the grace of his mother’s nurture, ennobled Yu’s wife Lady Wang as Mistress of Yinyang county and his maternal aunt, the wife of Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary Prince Xinye Wang Han, as Mistress of Pingyang township.
translations.idiomatic: In the Taining years, Emperor Ming remembered how his mother had raised him and invested Yu’s widow, Lady Wang, as Mistress of Yinyang county, and his aunt—the wife of Wang Han, Prince of Xinye and Regular Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary—as Mistress of Pingyang township.

sentences.zh: 荀豫章君

translations.literal: Lady Xun of Yuzhang (honorific title).
translations.idiomatic: Lady Xun of Yuzhang

sentences.zh: 豫章君荀氏，元帝宮人也。

translations.literal: The Yuzhang Lady Xun, of the Xun clan, was a palace woman of Emperor Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Xun of Yuzhang, from the Xun family, had entered Emperor Yuan’s harem.

sentences.zh: 初有寵，生明帝及琅邪王裒，由是為虞后所忌。

translations.literal: At first she enjoyed favor and bore Emperor Ming and Prince of Langya Sima Pou; on this account she was envied by Empress Yu.
translations.idiomatic: She was favored early on and gave birth to Emperor Ming and Sima Pou, Prince of Langya, which drew the jealousy of Empress Yu.

sentences.zh: 自以位卑，每懷怨望，為帝所譴，漸見疏薄。

translations.literal: Considering her own rank low, she constantly harbored resentment and was rebuked by the Emperor, and gradually came to be estranged and slighted.
translations.idiomatic: Conscious of her low standing, she nursed grievances until the emperor reproached her; thereafter he grew steadily cooler toward her.

sentences.zh: 及明帝即位，封建安君，別立第宅。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming ascended, she was enfeoffed as Lady of Jian’an and a separate residence was established for her.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Ming took the throne, he created her Lady of Jian’an and set aside a private mansion for her.

sentences.zh: 太寧元年，帝迎還臺內，供奉隆厚。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taining, the Emperor welcomed her back within the terrace compound, and her provision and honor were lavish.
translations.idiomatic: In 323 he brought her back into the palace precincts and treated her with exceptional generosity.

sentences.zh: 及成帝立，尊重同于太后。

translations.literal: When Emperor Cheng was established, she was honored and respected the same as an empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Cheng she was deferred to as if she were the empress dowager herself.

sentences.zh: 咸康元年薨。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xiankang she died.
translations.idiomatic: She died in 335.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「朕少遭憫凶，慈訓無稟，撫育之勤，建安君之仁也。

translations.literal: An edict stated: “In my youth I met with cruel bereavement; I received no kindly instruction; the toil of rearing me was the benevolence of the Lady of Jian’an.”
translations.idiomatic: The edict read: “I lost my parents while young and had no mother’s guidance; it was Lady of Jian’an who tirelessly raised me—that was her kindness.”

sentences.zh: 一旦薨殂，實思報復，永惟平昔，感痛哀摧。

translations.literal: Once she has died, I truly wish to repay her; forever pondering former days, I am moved to pain and grief-stricken.
translations.idiomatic: Now that she is gone, I long to repay her; when I think back on those years, sorrow overwhelms me.

sentences.zh: 其贈豫章郡君，別立廟于京都。」

translations.literal: “Let her be posthumously invested as Mistress of Yuzhang commandery, and let a separate temple be erected in the capital.”
translations.idiomatic: “Posthumously invest her as Mistress of Yuzhang commandery and build her an independent shrine in the capital.”

sentences.zh: 明穆庾皇后

translations.literal: Empress Yu, posthumous epithet Mingmu (“Clear and Solemn”).
translations.idiomatic: Empress Yu the Solemn and Clear-minded

sentences.zh: 明穆庾皇后諱文君，潁川鄢陵人也。

translations.literal: The Mingmu Empress Yu’s taboo name was Wenjun; she was a native of Yanling in Yingchuan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Yu the Solemn, whose personal name was Wenjun, hailed from Yanling in Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 父琛，見《外戚傳》。

translations.literal: Her father was Chen; see the “Biographies of the Consort Families.”
translations.idiomatic: Her father was Yu Chen; see the consort-kin biographies.

sentences.zh: 后性仁慈，美姿儀。

translations.literal: The empress by nature was humane and kind, and lovely in bearing.
translations.idiomatic: She was gentle and kind by nature, and strikingly graceful.

sentences.zh: 元帝聞之，聘為太子妃，以德行見重。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yuan heard of her, he engaged her as crown princess, and she was esteemed for virtue and conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan, hearing of her reputation, chose her as his heir’s consort; she was valued for character and deportment.

sentences.zh: 明帝即位，立為皇后。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming ascended, she was established as empress.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming took the throne, he made her empress.

sentences.zh: 冊曰：「妃庾氏昔承明命，作嬪東宮，虔恭中饋，思媚軌則。

translations.literal: The patent read: “Consort Yu formerly received the bright command, became consort in the Eastern Palace, reverently managed the inner quarters, and sought to please and follow the norms.”
translations.idiomatic: The investiture declared: “Lady Yu once accepted the imperial charge and entered the Eastern Palace as consort; she kept the inner household with devotion and strove to embody every duty expected of a wife.”

sentences.zh: 履信思順，以成肅雝之道；

translations.literal: Practicing good faith and thinking of compliance, thereby completing the way of solemn harmony;
translations.idiomatic: She walked in good faith and humility, fulfilling that harmonious virtue praised in the songs;

sentences.zh: 正位閨房，以著協德之美。

translations.literal: Correctly occupying the inner chambers, thereby displaying the beauty of coordinated virtue.
translations.idiomatic: She held her rightful place in the women’s quarters and showed what it means for spouses to match each other in virtue.

sentences.zh: 朕夙罹不造，煢煢在疚。

translations.literal: I early met ill fortune; alone I am in mourning.
translations.idiomatic: I have known bereavement from youth and stand orphaned in grief.

sentences.zh: 群公卿士，稽之往代，僉以崇嫡明統，載在典謨，宜建長秋，以奉宗廟。

translations.literal: The assembled dukes and gentlemen, examining past ages, all hold that exalting the principal line and clarifying the succession, recorded in the canonical counsels, requires establishing the empress of Changqiu to serve the ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: My ministers, looking to precedent, agree that raising the legitimate heir and securing the line—as the classics demand—means installing a chief consort worthy to assist the ancestral cult.

sentences.zh: 是以追述先志，不替舊命，使使持節兼太尉授皇后璽綬。

translations.literal: Therefore I pursue and narrate former intent, not replacing the old command, and dispatch a credential-bearing envoy concurrently Grand Commandant to confer the empress’s seal-cords.
translations.idiomatic: I therefore honor my late father’s wish and renew the earlier appointment, sending a credential-bearing Grand Commandant to invest you with the empress’s seals and ribbons.

sentences.zh: 夫坤德尚柔，婦道承姑，崇粢盛之禮，敦螽斯之義。

translations.literal: Now, the virtue of Earth esteems softness; the wife’s way receives the mother-in-law; exalt the rites of pure grain offerings; encourage the meaning of ‘many locusts’ (numerous offspring).
translations.idiomatic: Earth’s virtue lies in yielding; a wife’s duty includes serving her husband’s mother; honor the sacrifices and cherish the blessing of abundant heirs.

sentences.zh: 是以利在永貞，克隆堂基，母儀天下，潛暢陰教。

translations.literal: Therefore benefit lies in enduring constancy, broadly enlarge the hall’s foundation, be mother-model to All Under Heaven, and silently extend inner-chamber instruction.
translations.idiomatic: Perseverance in virtue will strengthen the dynasty; as mother of the realm, let your quiet influence spread the teaching of the inner quarters.

sentences.zh: 鑒于六列，考之篇籍，禍福無門，盛衰由人，雖休勿休。

translations.literal: Take mirror from the Six Ranks; examine the written records—fortune and calamity have no fixed gate; flourishing and decline depend on persons; though there be good fortune, do not treat it as repose.
translations.idiomatic: Read the lesson of the six grades of consorts and the histories: fortune follows no single path; rise and fall rest on human conduct; even in prosperity, never grow complacent.

sentences.zh: 其敬之哉，可不慎歟！」

translations.literal: Revere this—how can you not be cautious!”
translations.idiomatic: Revere these charges—could anything demand greater care?”

sentences.zh: 成恭杜皇后

translations.literal: Empress Du, posthumous epithets Cheng and Gong (“Accomplished and Reverent”).
translations.idiomatic: Empress Du the Accomplished and Reverent

sentences.zh: 成恭杜皇后諱陵陽[2]，京兆人，鎮南將軍預之曾孫也。

translations.literal: The Cheng-Gong Empress Du’s taboo name was Lingyang [note 2]; she was a person of the capital region and great-granddaughter of General Who Guards the South Du Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Du the Accomplished and Reverent, whose personal name was Lingyang, came from the Jingzhao area; she was a great-granddaughter of Du Yu, General Who Guards the South.

sentences.zh: 父乂，見《外戚傳》。

translations.literal: Her father was Yi; see the “Biographies of the Consort Families.”
translations.idiomatic: Her father was Du Yi; his biography appears among the consort kin.

sentences.zh: 成帝以后奕世名德，咸康二年備禮拜為皇后，即日入宮。

translations.literal: Emperor Cheng, on account of the empress’s house being illustrious in virtue through successive generations, in the second year of Xiankang with full rites invested her as empress, and the same day she entered the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Because her clan had been noted for virtue for generations, Emperor Cheng in 336 invested her as empress with full ceremony, and she moved into the palace that very day.

sentences.zh: 帝御太極前殿，群臣畢賀，晝漏盡，懸籥，百官乃罷。

translations.literal: The Emperor presided in the front hall of Taiji; the host of ministers all congratulated; when the day’s clepsydra ran out, the key was hung and the hundred officials then dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor received the court in the Taiji Hall’s forward chamber; after the full ritual of felicitations, the water-clock ran dry, the palace gates were sealed for the night, and the officials withdrew.

sentences.zh: 后少有姿色，然長猶無齒，有來求婚者輒中止。

translations.literal: The empress in youth had comely looks, yet grown she still lacked teeth; whenever suitors came, they always broke off.
translations.idiomatic: She had been pretty as a girl, but even when grown she still had no teeth, so every match that was proposed fell through.

sentences.zh: 及帝納采之日，一夜齒盡生。

translations.literal: When the day came for the Emperor’s betrothal gifts, in one night all her teeth grew.
translations.idiomatic: On the night before the formal betrothal, her teeth came in all at once.

sentences.zh: 改宣城陵陽縣為廣陽縣。

translations.literal: Lingyang county in Xuancheng was renamed Guangyang county.
translations.idiomatic: The county of Lingyang in Xuancheng was redesignated Guangyang, to avoid writing her name.

sentences.zh: 七年三月，后崩，年二十一。

translations.literal: In the third month of the seventh year she died; she was twenty-one sui.
translations.idiomatic: She died in the third month of 341, at twenty-one.

sentences.zh: 外官五日一臨，內官旦一入，葬訖止。

translations.literal: Outer officials were to attend mourning once every five days; inner officials once each morning; when burial was complete it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Outer-court officials were to visit the bier every fifth day, inner staff every morning, until the funeral ended.

sentences.zh: 后在位六年，無子。

translations.literal: The empress was on the throne six years; she had no sons.
translations.idiomatic: She had been empress for six years and bore no children.

sentences.zh: 先是，三吳女子相與簪白花，望之如素柰，傳言天公織女死，為之著服，至是而后崩。

translations.literal: Earlier, women of the three Wu regions together pinned white flowers, and gazing at them it was like white crabapples; rumor said the Weaver Girl of Heaven had died, and they wore mourning for her—thereupon the empress died.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, women east of the capital had taken to wearing white blossoms so thick they looked like drifts of pale crabapple; gossip said heaven’s Weaver Star had died and they were in mourning for her—then the empress passed away.

sentences.zh: 帝下詔曰：「吉凶典儀，誠宜備設；

translations.literal: The Emperor issued an edict stating: “For auspicious and inauspicious ritual models, it is truly fitting they be fully provided;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor decreed: “Funeral rites ought to be complete in form;

sentences.zh: 然豐約之度，亦當隨時，況重壤之下，而崇飾無用邪！

translations.literal: yet the measure of abundance and restraint should also follow the times—moreover beneath the heavy earth, to lavish useless ornament!”
translations.idiomatic: but scale should suit the times. How can we pile useless finery on someone who lies deep under the soil?”

sentences.zh: 今山陵之事，一從節儉，陵中唯潔掃而已，不得施塗車芻靈。

translations.literal: Now for the mausoleum affair, everything follows frugality; within the tumulus only pure sweeping—straw carriages and straw spirit-figures must not be deployed.”
translations.idiomatic: For her tomb, let everything be spare: the chamber need only be swept clean—no straw carriages or straw effigies.”

sentences.zh: 」有司奏造凶門柏歷及調挽郎，皆不許。

translations.literal: ” The responsible officials memorialized to construct the funeral gate, cypress sheds, and to levy pallbearers—all were disallowed.
translations.idiomatic: When officials asked to build the usual funeral gate and cypress biers and to draft professional mourners, he refused every request.

sentences.zh: 又禁遠近遣使。

translations.literal: Further, near and far envoys were forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: He also barred localities from sending delegations.

sentences.zh: 明年元會，有司奏廢樂。

translations.literal: The next year at the New Year court assembly, the responsible officials memorialized to abolish music.
translations.idiomatic: At the following New Year audience, the ministry asked to cancel the musical program.

sentences.zh: 詔廢管絃，奏金石如故。

translations.literal: An edict abolished strings and winds; metal and stone percussion was performed as before.
translations.idiomatic: He allowed only bells and chimes—strings and winds were dropped.

sentences.zh: 孝武帝立，寧康二年，以后母裴氏為廣德縣君。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu was established, in the second year of Ningkang he made the empress’s mother Lady Pei Mistress of Guangde county.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Xiaowu came to the throne, in 374 he ennobled the late empress’s mother, Lady Pei, as Mistress of Guangde county.

sentences.zh: 裴氏名穆，長水校尉綽孫，太傅主簿遐女，太尉王夷甫外孫。

translations.literal: The Pei clan lady’s name was Mu; she was granddaughter of Colonel of the Chang Waters Chuo, daughter of Grand Tutor chief clerk Xia, and maternal granddaughter of Grand Commandant Wang Yan (Yifu).
translations.idiomatic: Lady Pei, personal name Mu, was the granddaughter of Pei Chuo, Colonel of the Chang Waters; her father was Pei Xia, senior clerk to the Grand Tutor; her mother was a daughter of Wang Yan, the Grand Commandant known as Yifu.

sentences.zh: 中表之美，高於當世。

translations.literal: The excellence of her maternal and paternal kin was high in the age.
translations.idiomatic: Her relatives on both sides were among the most distinguished families of the day.

sentences.zh: 遐隨東海王越遇害，無子。

translations.literal: Xia followed Prince of the Eastern Sea Sima Yue and met murder; he had no sons.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Xia had been killed while in Sima Yue’s train and left no male heir.

sentences.zh: 唯穆渡江，遂享榮慶，立第南掖門外，世所謂杜姥宅云。

translations.literal: Only Mu crossed the Yangzi, thereupon enjoying glory and felicity; a mansion was erected outside the southern ye gate—what the age calls Granny Du’s house.
translations.idiomatic: Only Lady Mu made the crossing south and lived to see honor and comfort; her house stood just outside the southern palace gate—the mansion people still called “Old Lady Du’s place.”

sentences.zh: 周太妃

translations.literal: Grand Consort Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Consort Zhou

sentences.zh: 章太妃周氏以選入成帝宮，有寵，生哀帝及海西公。

translations.literal: Grand Consort Zhang, Lady Zhou, by selection entered Emperor Cheng’s palace, enjoyed favor, and bore Emperor Ai and the Prince of the Sea’s West.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Zhou, titled Grand Consort of Zhang, had entered Emperor Cheng’s harem as a chosen attendant; favored, she gave birth to Emperor Ai and Sima Yi, the Prince of Haixi.

sentences.zh: 始拜為貴人。

translations.literal: At first she was invested as Honored Person.
translations.idiomatic: She was first ranked as a noble lady.

sentences.zh: 哀帝即位，詔有司議貴人位號，太尉桓溫議宜稱夫人，尚書僕射江虨議應曰太夫人。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ai ascended, an edict ordered the responsible officials to deliberate the Honored Person’s title; Grand Commandant Huan Wen argued she ought to be styled Lady; Vice Director of the Secretariat Jiang Bin argued she should be called Grand Lady.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Ai took the throne, he told officials to fix a proper title for her: Huan Wen, as Grand Commandant, proposed “Lady”; Jiang Bin, Vice Director of the Secretariat, argued for “Grand Lady.”

sentences.zh: 詔崇為皇太妃，儀服與太后同。

translations.literal: An edict exalted her as imperial grand consort; ritual garb was the same as an empress dowager’s.
translations.idiomatic: The throne instead elevated her to imperial grand consort, with regalia matching an empress dowager’s.

sentences.zh: 又詔「朝臣不為太妃敬，合禮典不」。

translations.literal: Further an edict [asked]: “Court officials not performing reverence toward the grand consort—does it accord with ritual canons or not?”
translations.idiomatic: Another edict posed the question: “If courtiers refuse to bow to the grand consort, does that satisfy the ritual code?”

sentences.zh: 太常江逌議「位號不極，不應盡敬」。

translations.literal: Minister of Ceremonies Jiang You argued: “Her rank and title are not supreme; full reverence ought not be required.”
translations.idiomatic: Jiang You, Minister of Ceremonies, replied that her title fell short of the highest rank, so the full obeisance owed a dowager was not appropriate.

sentences.zh: 興寧元年薨。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xingning she died.
translations.idiomatic: She died in 363.

sentences.zh: 帝欲服重，江虨啟應緦麻三月。

translations.literal: The Emperor wished to wear heavy mourning; Jiang Bin stated he should wear fine hemp three months.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wanted to observe the heaviest mourning; Jiang Bin advised the three-month fine-hemp obligation instead.

sentences.zh: 詔欲降為期年，虨又啟「厭屈私情，所以上嚴祖考」，帝從之。

translations.literal: An edict wished to reduce it to one-year mourning; Bin further stated “suppressing and bending private feeling is thereby to show utmost respect to ancestors,” and the Emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: When the court suggested cutting it to one year, Jiang Bin argued that restraining private grief showed proper reverence toward the imperial ancestors; the emperor accepted his view.

sentences.zh: 康獻褚皇后

translations.literal: Empress Chu, posthumous epithets Kang and Xian (“Secure and Exemplary”).
translations.idiomatic: Empress Chu the Secure and Exemplary

sentences.zh: 康獻褚皇后諱蒜子，河南陽翟人也。

translations.literal: The Kang-Xian Empress Chu’s taboo name was Suànzi; she was a native of Yangzhai in Henan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Chu the Secure and Exemplary, whose personal name was Suanzi, came from Yangzhai in Henan.

sentences.zh: 父裒，見《外戚傳》。

translations.literal: Her father was Pou; see the “Biographies of the Consort Families.”
translations.idiomatic: Her father was Chu Pou; see the consort-kin section.

sentences.zh: 后聰明有器識，少以名家入為琅邪王妃。

translations.literal: The empress was intelligent and had capacity and insight; in youth, as one from a noted house, she entered to become Princess of Langya.
translations.idiomatic: She was bright and judicious, and as a girl from a great clan became consort to the Prince of Langya.

sentences.zh: 及康帝即位，立為皇后，封母謝氏為尋陽鄉君。

translations.literal: When Emperor Kang ascended, she was established as empress; her mother Lady Xie was enfeoffed Mistress of Xunyang township.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Kang succeeded, he made her empress and invested her mother, Lady Xie, as Mistress of Xunyang township.

sentences.zh: 及穆帝即位，尊后曰皇太后。

translations.literal: When Emperor Mu ascended, the empress was honored as empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Mu came to the throne, she was honored as empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 時帝幼沖，未親國政。

translations.literal: At that time the Emperor was young and in minority; he had not personally taken state government.
translations.idiomatic: The boy emperor was too young to rule in his own right.

sentences.zh: 領司徒蔡謨等上奏曰：「嗣皇誕哲岐嶷，繼承天統，率土宅心，兆庶蒙賴。

translations.literal: Acting Minister of Education Cai Mo and others presented a memorial stating: “The succeeding Emperor is born wise and precocious, inheriting Heaven’s line; within the Four Seas all anchor their hearts; the myriad people receive reliance.”
translations.idiomatic: Cai Mo, acting as Minister of Education, led a memorial: “The young sovereign is precocious and fit for the Mandate; the realm already looks to him and the people depend on his reign.”

sentences.zh: 陛下體茲坤道，訓隆文母。

translations.literal: Your Majesty embodies this Earth way; instruction exalts the mother of culture.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty embodies the yielding power of Earth and carries forward the teaching of King Wen’s mother.

sentences.zh: 昔塗山光夏，簡狄熙殷，實由宣哲，以隆休祚。

translations.literal: Formerly Tushan glorified Xia, Jiandi brightened Yin—truly by spreading wisdom they enlarged auspicious fortune.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient consorts of Yu and of Shang’s house brought glory to their dynasties through wisdom—such virtue magnifies the throne’s blessing.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下德侔二媯，淑美關雎，臨朝攝政，以寧天下。

translations.literal: We humbly consider that Your Majesty’s virtue matches the two Gui, chaste and lovely as ‘Guanju’; facing the court and holding the regency thereby pacifies All Under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: We beg you: your virtue rivals the consorts of Shun; your grace recalls the ode ‘Guanju.’ Take the regency and steady the realm.

sentences.zh: 今社稷危急，兆庶懸命，臣等章惶，一日萬機，事運之期，天祿所鍾，非復沖虛高讓之日。

translations.literal: Now altars and grain gods are perilous; the myriad people hang their lives—we ministers are anxious; in a day ten thousand threads of business; the period when affairs turn is where Heaven’s stipend concentrates—it is no longer a time for youthful modesty and lofty yielding.
translations.idiomatic: The altars are in peril and every life hangs in the balance; we ministers tremble at the myriad decisions a single day brings. This is the moment Heaven has chosen—no time for demurring modesty.

sentences.zh: 漢和熹、順烈，並亦臨朝，近明穆故事，以為先制。

translations.literal: Han’s He Xi and Shun Lie both likewise faced the court; the recent Mingmu precedent is taken as former regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Han’s Deng and Liang empresses both governed from behind the screen; our own late Empress Yu the Solemn offers the nearest precedent.

sentences.zh: 臣等不勝悲怖，謹伏地上請。

translations.literal: We ministers cannot bear grief and fear; respectfully we prostrate on the ground and request.
translations.idiomatic: Overcome with fear and sorrow, we prostrate ourselves and implore you.

sentences.zh: 乞陛下上順祖宗，下念臣吏，推公弘道，以協天人，則萬邦承慶，群黎更生。

translations.literal: We beg Your Majesty above to comply with ancestors, below to think on ministers and clerks; extend impartiality and enlarge the Way, thereby harmonizing Heaven and man—then the myriad regions will receive blessing and the masses will gain new life.”
translations.idiomatic: Honor the ancestors, remember your officials, and rule with impartial sagacity so Heaven and humanity align; every state will rejoice and the people will be reborn from peril.

sentences.zh: 」太后詔曰：「帝幼沖，當賴群公卿士將順匡救，以酬先帝禮賢之意，且是舊德世濟之美，則莫重之命不墜，祖宗之基有奉，是其所以欲正位于內而已。

translations.literal: The empress dowager’s edict stated: “The Emperor is young and in minority; he ought to rely on the assembled dukes and gentlemen to lead compliance and rescue, thereby repaying the late Emperor’s intent to honor the worthy; moreover it is the beauty of old virtue aiding generation after generation—then the supremely weighty Mandate does not fall, and the ancestors’ foundation has one to uphold it—this alone is the reason for desiring to correct position within.”
translations.idiomatic: The dowager replied: “The emperor is a child; he must lean on you ministers to guide and correct the court—that fulfills his late father’s wish to honor worthy men. Our house’s accumulated virtue must not let the great Mandate slip; someone must guard the ancestral enterprise. That is all I mean by wishing to settle rightful authority within the palace.”

sentences.zh: 所奏懇到，形于翰墨，執省未究，以悲以懼。

translations.literal: What was memorialized was earnest and thorough, formed in brush and ink; holding and examining, not yet exhausted—I am both grieved and fearful.
translations.idiomatic: Your words are earnest and fill page after page; as I read them through, grief and apprehension mingle.

sentences.zh: 先后允恭謙抑，思順坤道，所以不距群情，固為國計。

translations.literal: The late empresses were truly deferential and modest, thinking to comply with the Earth way; therefore they did not reject the multitude’s feelings—solidly for the state’s plan.
translations.idiomatic: My predecessors were humble and yielded to circumstance in the spirit of Earth; they did not refuse the court’s pleas when the realm required it.

sentences.zh: 豈敢執守沖闇，以違先旨。

translations.literal: How dare I cling to youthful obscurity, thereby contravening former intent?
translations.idiomatic: I cannot cling to youthful modesty and defy what those before me intended.

sentences.zh: 輒敬從所奏。

translations.literal: I respectfully follow what was memorialized.
translations.idiomatic: I accept your request.

sentences.zh: 」於是臨朝稱制。

translations.literal: Thereupon she faced the court and assumed regnal authority.
translations.idiomatic: With that, she held court and issued orders in the emperor’s name.

sentences.zh: 有司奏，謝夫人既封，荀、卞二夫人亦應追贈，皆后之前母也。

translations.literal: The responsible officials memorialized: since Lady Xie has been enfeoffed, the two ladies Xun and Bian also ought to receive posthumous gifts—all were the empress’s former mothers.
translations.idiomatic: Officials noted that Lady Xie had received a title and asked that Lady Xun and Lady Bian—the empress’s two stepmothers—be honored posthumously as well.

sentences.zh: 太后不許。

translations.literal: The empress dowager did not permit.
translations.idiomatic: The dowager refused.

sentences.zh: 太常殷融議依鄭玄義，衛將軍裒在宮庭則盡臣敬，太后歸寧之日自如家人之禮。

translations.literal: Minister of Ceremonies Yin Rong argued following Zheng Xuan’s interpretation: when General Who Guards the Army Pou is in the palace precincts, then exhaust ministerial reverence; on days when the empress dowager returns in peace to her family, naturally use family-member rites.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Rong, Minister of Ceremonies, cited Zheng Xuan: Chu Pou should observe full court etiquette while at court, but when the dowager visited her family home, they could behave as ordinary kin.

sentences.zh: 太后詔曰：「典禮誠所未詳，如所奏，是情所不能安也，更詳之。

translations.literal: The empress dowager’s edict stated: “The canonical rites are indeed not yet clear in this; as memorialized, that is what feeling cannot rest with—reconsider it further.”
translations.idiomatic: The dowager replied: “The classics do not spell this out clearly; your proposal would leave me uneasy. Think it through again.”

sentences.zh: 」征西將軍翼、南中郎尚議謂「父尊盡於一家，君敬重於天下，鄭玄義合情禮之中」。

translations.literal: ” General Who Conquers the West Yu Yi and South Household Gentlemen Yu Shang argued that “a father’s honor is exhausted within one family, while a lord’s reverence extends across All Under Heaven; Zheng Xuan’s reading hits the mean of feeling and rite.”
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yi, the western expedition commander, and Yu Shang, South Household Gentlemen, cited Zheng Xuan: paternal authority stops at the household, whereas the ruler’s dignity belongs to the realm—their view balanced duty and affection.”

sentences.zh: 太后從之。

translations.literal: The empress dowager followed it.
translations.idiomatic: The dowager accepted their opinion.

sentences.zh: 自後朝臣皆敬裒焉。

translations.literal: Thereafter court ministers all showed reverence to Pou.
translations.idiomatic: After that, every courtier treated Chu Pou with the full deference due a minister.

sentences.zh: 帝既冠，太后詔曰：「昔遭不造，帝在幼沖，皇緒之微，眇若贅旒。

translations.literal: After the capping ceremony, the empress dowager’s edict stated: “Formerly we met ill fortune; the Emperor was in minority; the imperial thread was as slight as dangling tassels.”
translations.idiomatic: Once the emperor came of age, the dowager proclaimed: “In those dark years the boy on the throne was all that stood between the dynasty and collapse.”

sentences.zh: 百辟卿士率遵前朝，勸喻攝政。

translations.literal: The hundred nobles and gentlemen all followed the former court and urged a regency.
translations.idiomatic: The high ministers, holding to precedent, pressed me to govern in his name.”

sentences.zh: 以社稷之重，先代成義，僶俛敬從，弗遑固守。

translations.literal: On account of the altars’ weight and the completed righteousness of former ages, I respectfully complied, not daring to cling to refusal.
translations.idiomatic: The altars left me no choice; I bowed to ancient example and took the regency, though I never wished to hold power for myself.”

sentences.zh: 仰憑七廟之靈，俯仗群后之力，帝加元服，禮成德備，當陽親覽，臨御萬國。

translations.literal: Relying above on the spirits of the seven temples, relying below on the strength of the host of lords, the Emperor has added the capping rite; the rites are complete and virtue prepared—he should face the south in person and oversee the myriad states.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven and our ancestors preserved us; with your help he has reached his majority and is ready to rule face-to-face with the realm.”

sentences.zh: 今歸事反政，一依舊典。

translations.literal: Now affairs return and government is handed back, wholly according to old statutes.
translations.idiomatic: I therefore return the government to him, following the old statutes to the letter.”

sentences.zh: 」于是居崇德宮，手詔群公曰：「昔以皇帝幼沖，從群后之議，既以闇弱，又頻丁極艱，銜恤歷祀，沈憂在疚。

translations.literal: ” Thereupon she resided in Chongde Palace and by handwritten edict told the assembled lords: “Formerly because the Emperor was young and in minority, I followed the lords’ deliberation; already benighted and weak, I also repeatedly met extreme hardship, bore grief through the years, and sank in sorrow within mourning.”
translations.idiomatic: She moved to Chongde Palace and sent a personal note to the great officers: “I took the regency only because he was a child; I am myself frail, and year after year of mourning and crisis have worn me down.”

sentences.zh: 司徒親尊德重，訓救其弊，王室之不壞，實公是憑。

translations.literal: The Minister of Education is kin of highest honor and virtue weighty; he corrected and rescued its ills—the royal house’s not being ruined truly depends on him.
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of Education, noble in both blood and character, steadied us when we faltered; the house of Sima owes him its survival.”

sentences.zh: 帝既備茲冠禮，而四海未一，五胡叛逆，豺狼當路，費役日興，百姓困苦。

translations.literal: The Emperor having completed this capping rite, yet the Four Seas are not unified, the five Hu rebel, wolves block the road, levies and labor rise daily, and the hundred surnames are distressed.
translations.idiomatic: He is a man grown, yet the empire is still torn: barbarian armies prowl the roads and the people stagger under endless exactions.”

sentences.zh: 願諸君子思量遠算，戮力一心，輔翼幼主，匡救不逮。

translations.literal: I hope you gentlemen will ponder far plans, join strength with one mind, wing the young lord, and rescue what is lacking.
translations.idiomatic: I ask you to look beyond the day, stand together, support the young sovereign, and mend every gap you find.”

sentences.zh: 未亡人永歸別宮，以終餘齒。

translations.literal: I, the not-yet-dead woman, forever return to a separate palace to finish my remaining years.
translations.idiomatic: I shall withdraw to another palace and live out what years remain to me.”

sentences.zh: 仰惟家國，故以一言託懷。」

translations.literal: Looking up I think on family and state; therefore with one phrase I entrust my feelings.”
translations.idiomatic: I mention this only because the realm and the clan weigh on my heart.”

sentences.zh: 及哀帝、海西公之世，太后復臨朝稱制[3]。

translations.literal: In the eras of Emperor Ai and the Prince of Haixi, the empress dowager again faced the court and assumed regnal authority [note 3].
translations.idiomatic: During the reigns of Emperor Ai and the deposed Prince of Haixi, she took up the regency once more.

sentences.zh: 桓溫之廢海西公也，太后方在佛屋燒香，內侍啟云「外有急奏」，太后乃出。

translations.literal: When Huan Wen deposed the Prince of Haixi, the empress dowager was just burning incense in the Buddha hall; an inner attendant reported “outside there is an urgent memorial,” and the empress dowager then came out.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen’s coup caught her at prayer in the chapel; a eunuch whispered that urgent papers had arrived, and she came out to receive them.

sentences.zh: 尚倚戶前視奏數行，乃曰「我本自疑此」，至半便止，索筆答奏云：「未亡人罹此百憂，感念存沒，心焉如割。

translations.literal: Leaning against the doorframe, she read several lines of the memorial, then said “I myself had suspected this”; halfway through she stopped, demanded a brush, and replied to the memorial stating: “I, the not-yet-dead woman, have met this hundredfold grief; thinking on the living and the dead, my heart is as if cut.”
translations.idiomatic: She skimmed the opening lines at her doorway and murmured that she had half expected the news; she broke off midway, took brush in hand, and wrote that widowhood had brought every sorrow imaginable and that her heart felt torn out.”

sentences.zh: 」溫始呈詔草，慮太后意異，悚動流汗，見于顏色。

translations.literal: ” When Huan Wen first presented the draft edict, he feared the empress dowager’s intent might differ; trembling, sweat flowed, visible in his expression.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen, presenting his draft abdication edict, was terrified she might balk—his face ran with sweat.”

sentences.zh: 及詔出，溫大喜。

translations.literal: When the edict issued, Huan Wen was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Once she sealed the document, Huan Wen was elated.

sentences.zh: 簡文帝即位，尊后為崇德太后。

translations.literal: When Emperor Jianwen ascended, she was honored as Chongde Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jianwen raised her to Grand Dowager of Chongde.

sentences.zh: 及帝崩，孝武帝幼沖，桓溫又薨。

translations.literal: When the Emperor died, Emperor Xiaowu was young and in minority, and Huan Wen also died.
translations.idiomatic: Jianwen soon died, leaving Xiaowu a minor; then Huan Wen died as well.

sentences.zh: 群臣啟曰：「王室多故，禍艱仍臻，國憂始周，復喪元輔，天下惘然，若無攸濟。

translations.literal: The host of ministers stated: “The royal house has many troubles; calamity and hardship repeatedly arrive; state grief has barely closed when we again lose the paramount minister—all Under Heaven is dazed, as if with none to ford across.”
translations.idiomatic: The ministers wrote: “Disaster has followed disaster; we have scarcely buried one sovereign before we lose our chief minister—the court is adrift.”

sentences.zh: 主上雖聖資奇茂，固天誕縱。

translations.literal: Although the lord above is sagely in endowment and wondrously abundant, indeed Heaven endowed him lavishly.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor is gifted beyond measure—Heaven has showered him with talent—but he is still a boy.

sentences.zh: 而春秋尚富，如在諒闇，蒸蒸之思，未遑庶事。

translations.literal: Yet his spring-and-autumn is still rich; he is as if within the hut of mourning; the steaming thoughts have not yet attended to the myriad affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He remains in deep mourning for his father and has no leisure yet for the business of state.”

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下德應坤厚，宣慈聖善，遭家多艱，臨朝親覽。

translations.literal: We humbly consider that Your Majesty’s virtue answers to Earth’s thickness, spreading kindness and sagely goodness; meeting the house’s many hardships, you faced the court and personally oversaw.
translations.idiomatic: We beg you, whose kindness matches the earth itself, to resume the regency you held when crises multiplied.”

sentences.zh: 光大之美，化洽在昔，謳歌流詠，播溢無外。

translations.literal: The beauty of enlarging and brightening, transforming harmony in former times, songs and chants flowing, spread abroad without limit.
translations.idiomatic: The glory you brought to the government in those years still fills every corner of the realm with praise.”

sentences.zh: 雖有莘熙殷，妊姒隆周，未足以喻。

translations.literal: Although there were the Xin who brightened Yin and the Si who enlarged Zhou, they are not enough for comparison.
translations.idiomatic: Not even the mothers of Shang and Zhou outshone your record.”

sentences.zh: 是以五謀克從，人鬼同心，仰望來蘇，懸心日月。

translations.literal: Therefore the five counsels were obeyed, man and ghost of one mind; looking up they hope for renewal, hearts hang on sun and moon.
translations.idiomatic: Every voice joined in pleading; high and low look to you as they would to the sun.”

sentences.zh: 夫隨時之義，周易所尚，寧固社稷，大人之任。

translations.literal: The meaning of following the times is what the Zhou Changes esteems; securing firm the altars is the great man’s charge.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Changes honors adapting to the hour; guarding the dynasty is the duty of those who lead.”

sentences.zh: 伏願陛下撫綜萬機，釐和政道，以慰祖宗，以安兆庶。

translations.literal: We humbly hope Your Majesty will handle the myriad threads, order and harmonize government ways, thereby comforting ancestors and settling the myriad people.
translations.idiomatic: Take the reins again, set policy to rights, comfort the ancestral spirits, and give the people peace.”

sentences.zh: 不勝憂國喁喁至誠。

translations.literal: We cannot bear the state’s worry, sincere to the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: We speak from urgent, heartfelt concern for the realm.”

sentences.zh: 」太后詔曰：「王室不幸，仍有艱屯。

translations.literal: ” The empress dowager’s edict stated: “The royal house is unlucky; still there are hard straits.”
translations.idiomatic: She answered: “The dynasty’s misfortunes are not yet over.”

sentences.zh: 覽省啟事，感增悲歎。

translations.literal: Reviewing the memorial, feeling increased grief and sighing.
translations.idiomatic: Your words add fresh sorrow to all I bear.”

sentences.zh: 內外諸君，並以主上春秋沖富，加蒸蒸之慕，未能親覽，號令宜有所由。

translations.literal: Inner and outer gentlemen all take it that the lord above’s spring-and-autumn is still flush, and with the addition of steaming longing, he is not yet able personally to oversee; commands ought to have a source.
translations.idiomatic: He is young and still wrapped in filial grief; someone must speak in his name.”

sentences.zh: 苟可安社稷，利天下，亦豈有所執，輒敬從所啟。

translations.literal: If it can secure the altars and benefit All Under Heaven, how could I cling to anything? I respectfully follow what was opened.”
translations.idiomatic: If returning to the regency steadies the state, I will not refuse—I accept.”

sentences.zh: 但闇昧之闕，望盡弼諧之道。

translations.literal: Only for benighted gaps, I hope fully for the way of assisting harmony.
translations.idiomatic: Where I am blind, rely on you to counsel and correct me.”

sentences.zh: 」於是太后復臨朝。

translations.literal: ” Thereupon the empress dowager again faced the court.
translations.idiomatic: With that she resumed the regency.

sentences.zh: 帝既冠，乃詔曰：「皇帝婚冠禮備，遐邇宅心，宜當陽親覽，緝熙惟始。

translations.literal: After the Emperor’s capping, then an edict stated: “The Emperor’s marriage and capping rites are complete; far and near anchor their hearts—he ought to face the south in person and begin brilliant rule.”
translations.idiomatic: When he had come of age and married, she decreed that the realm expected him to take personal command and begin his own reign.”

sentences.zh: 今歸政事，率由舊典。

translations.literal: Now government affairs return, following entirely the old canons.
translations.idiomatic: She returned all authority and held to precedent.”

sentences.zh: 」於是復稱崇德太后。

translations.literal: ” Thereupon she was again titled Chongde Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: She was again styled Grand Dowager of Chongde.

sentences.zh: 太元九年，崩于顯陽殿，年六十一，在位凡四十年。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Taiyuan she died in Xianyang Hall; she was sixty-one sui; her time in position totaled forty years.
translations.idiomatic: She died in 384 in Xianyang Hall, aged sixty-one, after forty years at the center of power.

sentences.zh: 太后於帝為從嫂，朝議疑其服。

translations.literal: To the Emperor the empress dowager was a cousin-in-law; court deliberation doubted her mourning garments.
translations.idiomatic: For Emperor Xiaowu she was a cousin’s widow, and ministers quarreled over what mourning he owed.

sentences.zh: 太學博士徐藻議曰：「資父事君而敬同。

translations.literal: Erudite of the Imperial Academy Xu Zao argued: “Serving the father and serving the lord share the same reverence.”
translations.idiomatic: Xu Zao of the National University cited the canon: reverence for father matches reverence for ruler.

sentences.zh: 又禮云『其夫屬父道者，妻皆母道也』，則夫屬君道，妻亦后道矣。

translations.literal: Moreover the rites state ‘When the husband belongs to the father’s way, the wife all belongs to the mother’s way’—then when the husband belongs to the lord’s way, the wife also belongs to the empress’s way.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual also says that when a husband stands in the place of a father to you, his wife stands as a mother—by the same token, a consort who acts as sovereign demands the mourning due a mother.”

sentences.zh: 服后以齊，母之義也。

translations.literal: Mourning the empress with aligned hemp is the meaning of ‘mother.’
translations.idiomatic: Therefore one wears the graded hemp for a mother toward her.”

sentences.zh: 魯譏逆祀，以明尊卑[4]。

translations.literal: Lu criticized inverse sacrifice to clarify high and low [note 4].
translations.idiomatic: Lu’s condemnation of improper sacrifice shows how rank must be kept straight.”

sentences.zh: 今上躬奉康、穆、哀皇及靖后之祀，致敬同于所天，豈可敬之以君道，而服廢於本親。

translations.literal: Now the sovereign personally performs sacrifice to Emperors Kang, Mu, and Ai and to Empress Jing, showing reverence the same as to their Heaven—how can one reverence them with the lord’s way yet wear mourning cut off toward close kin?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor already honors Kang, Mu, Ai, and Empress Jing as he would his lords—he cannot treat them as rulers in the temple yet shirk kinship mourning for the woman who stood as his mother in law.”

sentences.zh: 謂應齊衰期。

translations.literal: It is fitting to wear hemmed sackcloth for one year.
translations.idiomatic: He should observe one year’s hemmed sackcloth.”

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: ” They followed it.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 穆章何皇后

translations.literal: Empress He, posthumous epithets Mu and Zhang.
translations.idiomatic: Empress He the Solemn and Illustrious

sentences.zh: 穆章何皇后諱法倪，廬江灊人也。

translations.literal: The Mu-Zhang Empress He’s taboo name was Fanni; she was a native of Qian in Lujiang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Empress He the Solemn and Illustrious, personal name Fanni, came from Qian in Lujiang.

sentences.zh: 父準，見《外戚傳》。

translations.literal: Her father was Zhun; see the “Biographies of the Consort Families.”
translations.idiomatic: Her father was He Zhun, recorded among the consort kin.

sentences.zh: 以名家膺選。

translations.literal: By noted house she was selected.
translations.idiomatic: She entered the selection as a daughter of a great clan.

sentences.zh: 升平元年八月，下璽書曰：「皇帝咨前太尉參軍何琦：混元資始，肇經人倫，爰及夫婦，以奉天地宗廟社稷。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the first year of Shengping, a jade patent stated: “The Emperor addresses former Army aide to the Grand Commandant He Qi: Primal chaos provides the beginning; it begins with human relations, extending to husband and wife, thereby serving Heaven and Earth, the ancestral temple, and the altars.”
translations.idiomatic: In 357 an imperial rescript addressed He Qi: marriage orders society and sustains the sacrifices to Heaven, earth, and ancestors.”

sentences.zh: 謀于公卿，咸以宜率由舊典。

translations.literal: Deliberating with dukes and ministers, all held it fitting to follow entirely the old canons.
translations.idiomatic: After consulting the ministers, all agreed the ancient betrothal rites should be followed.”

sentences.zh: 今使使持節太常彪之、宗正綜，以禮納采。

translations.literal: Now I dispatch credential-bearing Minister of Ceremonies Wang Biaozhi and Director of the Imperial Clan Wang Zong to take the rites and present betrothal gifts.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore sent Wang Biaozhi and Wang Zong, with credentials, to perform the betrothal ceremony.”

sentences.zh: 」琦答曰：「前太尉參軍、都鄉侯糞土臣何琦稽首頓首再拜。

translations.literal: ” Qi replied: “Former Army aide to the Grand Commandant, Marquis of Duxiang, dung-soil subject He Qi bows head, touches head, twice prostrates.”
translations.idiomatic: He Qi answered with the prescribed self-abasing formula accepting the imperial command.”

sentences.zh: 皇帝嘉命，訪婚陋族，備數採擇。

translations.literal: The Emperor’s fine command inquires marriage with my humble clan, fully numbering among selection.
translations.idiomatic: He thanked the throne for deigning to seek a bride among his kin.”

sentences.zh: 臣從祖弟故散騎侍郎準之遺女，未閑教訓，衣履若如人。

translations.literal: My paternal cousin’s late daughter, former Cavalier for Regular Attendance Zhun’s orphaned girl, is not yet versed in instruction and training; her dress and shoes are like a person’s.
translations.idiomatic: He offered his cousin’s daughter, the child left by the late He Zhun, still untrained but presentable.”

sentences.zh: 欽承舊章，肅奉典制。

translations.literal: I reverently receive the old statutes and solemnly uphold the canonical system.”
translations.idiomatic: He pledged to observe every detail of ritual.”

sentences.zh: 」又使兼太保、武陵王晞，兼太尉、中領軍洽，持節奉冊立為皇后。

translations.literal: ” Further he dispatched concurrent Grand Guardian Prince of Wuling Sima Xi and concurrent Grand Commandant Central Army commander Wang Qia, bearing credentials, to present the patent and establish her as empress.
translations.idiomatic: The court then sent Sima Xi and Wang Qia to invest her as empress with the formal patent.”

sentences.zh: 后無子。

translations.literal: The empress had no sons.
translations.idiomatic: She bore no children.

sentences.zh: 哀帝即位，稱穆皇后，居永安宮。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ai ascended, she was titled Empress Mu and resided in Yong’an Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ai styled her Empress Mu and installed her in Yong’an Palace.

sentences.zh: 桓玄篡位，移后入司徒府。

translations.literal: When Huan Xuan usurped the throne, he moved the empress into the Minister of Education’s office.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan, seizing power, quartered her in the ministry compound.

sentences.zh: 路經太廟，后停輿慟哭，哀感路人。

translations.literal: Passing the Grand Temple, the empress halted the carriage and wailed in grief, sorrow moving wayfarers.
translations.idiomatic: As her cart passed the imperial temple she stopped and wept until bystanders wept with her.

sentences.zh: 玄聞而怒曰：「天下禪代常理，何預何氏女子事耶！

translations.literal: Xuan heard and angrily said: “All Under Heaven’s abdication and replacement is constant principle—what does it concern a woman of the He clan!”
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan snarled that dynastic change was none of a He woman’s business.”

sentences.zh: 」乃降后為零陵縣君。

translations.literal: ” Thereupon he demoted the empress to Mistress of Lingling county.
translations.idiomatic: He reduced her to Mistress of Lingling.

sentences.zh: 與安帝俱西，至巴陵。

translations.literal: Together with Emperor An she went west, reaching Baling.
translations.idiomatic: She accompanied Emperor An westward as far as Baling.

sentences.zh: 及劉裕建義，殷仲文奉后還京都，下令曰：「戎車屢警，黎元阻饑。

translations.literal: When Liu Yu raised righteous arms, Yin Zhongwen escorted the empress back to the capital; an order stated: “War chariots have repeatedly alarmed; the black-haired folk are blocked and starving.”
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yu rose against Huan, Yin Zhongwen brought her home; an edict cited the war weariness and famine in the land.”

sentences.zh: 而膳御豐靡，豈與百姓同其儉約。

translations.literal: Yet imperial kitchens are abundant and extravagant—how can that share frugality with the hundred surnames?
translations.idiomatic: Yet palace fare remained lavish—hardly an example of austerity for the people.”

sentences.zh: 減損供給，勿令游過。

translations.literal: Reduce and cut supplies; do not let them exceed.”
translations.idiomatic: Cut court provisioning and forbid excess.”

sentences.zh: 」后時以遠還，欲奉拜陵廟。

translations.literal: ” At that time the empress, having returned from afar, wished to perform obeisance at the mausoleum temples.
translations.idiomatic: The empress, newly returned, asked to worship at the imperial tombs.”

sentences.zh: 有司以寇難未平，奏停。

translations.literal: The responsible officials, because bandit difficulty was not yet pacified, memorialized to stop.
translations.idiomatic: Officials refused, citing the ongoing rebellion.

sentences.zh: 元興三年崩[5]，年六十六，在位凡四十八年。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yuanxing she died [note 5]; she was sixty-six sui; her time in position totaled forty-eight years.
translations.idiomatic: She died in 404 at sixty-six, after forty-eight years as consort or empress.

sentences.zh: 哀靖王皇后

translations.literal: Empress Wang, posthumous epithets Ai and Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wang the Lamented and Serene

sentences.zh: 廢帝孝庾皇后

translations.literal: Empress Yu, posthumous epithet Xiao, of the deposed Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Yu the Filial, wife of the deposed emperor

sentences.zh: 廢帝孝庾皇后諱道憐，潁川鄢陵人也。

translations.literal: The deposed Emperor’s Xiao Empress Yu’s taboo name was Daolian; she was a native of Yanling in Yingchuan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Yu the Filial, personal name Daolian, came from Yanling in Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 父冰，自有傳。

translations.literal: Her father was Bing; he has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Her father was Yu Bing, who has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 初為東海王妃。

translations.literal: At first she was Princess of the Eastern Sea.
translations.idiomatic: She began as consort to the Prince of the Eastern Sea.

sentences.zh: 及帝即位，立為皇后。

translations.literal: When the Emperor ascended, she was established as empress.
translations.idiomatic: When he took the throne, she became empress.

sentences.zh: 太和六年崩[6]，葬于敬平陵。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Taihe she died [note 6] and was buried at Jingping Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: She died in 371 and was buried at Jingping Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 帝廢為海西公，追貶后曰海西公夫人。

translations.literal: The Emperor was deposed as Prince of Haixi; she was posthumously demoted and titled Lady of the Prince of Haixi.
translations.idiomatic: When he was demoted to Prince of Haixi, she was stripped of her rank and titled merely his consort.

sentences.zh: 太元十一年，海西公薨于吳[7]，又以后合葬于吳陵。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Taiyuan the Prince of Haixi died in Wu [note 7]; later she was jointly buried with him at Wu Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: When he died in Wu in 386, she was later reinterred with him at the Wu tomb complex.

sentences.zh: 簡文宣鄭太后

translations.literal: Dowager Empress Zheng, posthumous epithets Jianwen and Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Dowager Zheng of Jianwen and the Exalted

sentences.zh: 簡文宣鄭太后諱阿春，河南滎陽人也。

translations.literal: The Jianwen-Xuan Dowager Zheng’s taboo name was Achun; she was a native of Xingyang in Henan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Dowager Zheng, personal name Achun, came from Xingyang in Henan.

sentences.zh: 世為冠族。

translations.literal: For generations they were a cap-and-girdle great clan.
translations.idiomatic: Her family had been eminent for generations.

sentences.zh: 祖合，臨濟令。

translations.literal: Her grandfather was He, magistrate of Linji.
translations.idiomatic: Her grandfather Zheng He had served as magistrate of Linji.

sentences.zh: 父愷，字祖元，安豐太守。

translations.literal: Her father was Kai, style Zuyuan, governor of Anfeng.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Zheng Kai, courtesy Zuyuan, was governor of Anfeng.

sentences.zh: 后少孤，無兄弟，唯姊妹四人，后最長。

translations.literal: The empress in youth was orphaned; she had no brothers, only four sisters, of whom she was eldest.
translations.idiomatic: She lost her parents early, had no brothers, and was the eldest of four sisters.

sentences.zh: 先適渤海田氏，生一男而寡，依于舅濮陽吳氏。

translations.literal: First she married into the Bohai Tian clan, bore one son, and was widowed; she relied on her maternal uncle’s Wu clan of Puyang.
translations.idiomatic: Her first marriage, to a man of Bohai’s Tian family, left her a widow with one son; she then lived with her uncle’s household in Puyang.

sentences.zh: 元帝為丞相，敬后先崩，將納吳氏女為夫人。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yuan was Chancellor, Empress Jing had died first; he was about to take a daughter of the Wu clan as lady.
translations.idiomatic: While still Prince of Langya and serving as chancellor, he had lost Empress Yu; he planned to take a Wu daughter as his consort.

sentences.zh: 后及吳氏女並游後園，或見之，言於帝曰：「鄭氏女雖嫠，賢於吳氏遠矣。

translations.literal: The empress and the Wu daughter together strolled the rear garden; someone saw them and spoke to the Emperor saying: “Though the Zheng lady is a widow, she is far worthier than the Wu girl.”
translations.idiomatic: Lady Zheng and the Wu maiden toured the rear garden together; an observer told him the widowed Zheng lady far outshone his intended bride.”

sentences.zh: 」建武元年，納為琅邪王夫人，甚有寵。

translations.literal: ” In the first year of Jianwu, she was taken in as Lady Wang, Prince of Langya, and greatly favored.
translations.idiomatic: In 317 he took her as his consort instead and favored her deeply.

sentences.zh: 后雖貴幸，而恒有憂色。

translations.literal: Although the empress was honored and favored, she constantly had a worried expression.
translations.idiomatic: Even at the height of favor she often looked troubled.

sentences.zh: 帝問其故，對曰：「妾有妹，中者已適長沙王褒，餘二妹未有所適，恐姊為人妾，無復求者。

translations.literal: The Emperor asked the reason; she replied: “I have younger sisters; the middle one has already married Prince of Changsha Bao; the remaining two have no matches—I fear that as elder sister I have become someone’s concubine, none will again seek them.”
translations.idiomatic: Asked why, she said her middle sister was already wife to Sima Bao, Prince of Changsha, while the other two were still unwed; she worried that because she herself was a concubine, no one would ask for them.”

sentences.zh: 」帝因從容謂劉隗曰：「鄭氏二妹，卿可為求佳對，使不失舊。

translations.literal: ” The Emperor therefore casually told Liu Wei: “Zheng’s two younger sisters—you may seek fine matches, so they do not lose their standing.”
translations.idiomatic: The prince quietly asked Liu Wei to find honorable husbands for the two younger girls.”

sentences.zh: 」隗舉其從子傭娶第三者，以小者適漢中李氏，皆得舊門。

translations.literal: ” Wei recommended his nephew Yong to marry the third; the youngest he matched to the Li clan of Hanzhong—all obtained old-line houses.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Wei gave his nephew Yong the third sister and married the youngest into the Li family of Hanzhong—both matches kept the girls within the elite.”

sentences.zh: 帝召王褒為尚書郎，以悅后意。

translations.literal: The Emperor summoned Wang Bao to be a gentleman of the Masters of Writing, to please the empress’s intent.
translations.idiomatic: To please her, he gave Wang Bao a post among the Masters of Writing secretaries.

sentences.zh: 后生琅邪悼王、簡文帝、尋陽公主。

translations.literal: The empress bore Prince of Langya the Lamented, Emperor Jianwen, and the Princess of Xunyang.
translations.idiomatic: She gave birth to the Prince of Langya who died young, to Emperor Jianwen, and to the Princess of Xunyang.

sentences.zh: 帝稱尊號，后雖為夫人，詔太子及東海、武陵王皆母事之。

translations.literal: When the Emperor assumed the exalted title, although the empress was still ranked as Lady, an edict ordered the crown prince and the Princes of the Eastern Sea and Wuling all to serve her as a mother.
translations.idiomatic: Once he took the throne, she remained a consort in rank, yet he commanded the heir apparent and the eastern princes to honor her as they would a mother.

sentences.zh: 帝崩，后稱建平國夫人。

translations.literal: When the Emperor died, she was titled Lady of the Jianping march.
translations.idiomatic: After his death she was known as Lady of the Jianping fief.

sentences.zh: 咸和元年薨，簡文帝時為琅邪王，制服重。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianhe she died; at the time Emperor Jianwen was Prince of Langya and wore heavy mourning.
translations.idiomatic: She died in 326 while Sima Yu was still Prince of Langya; he observed the full mourning grade.

sentences.zh: 有司以王出繼，宜降所生，國臣不能匡正，奏免國相諸葛頤。

translations.literal: The responsible officials held that because the prince had been given out in succession to another line, mourning toward his birth parent ought to be reduced; the march ministers could not correct this, and they memorialized to dismiss march minister Zhuge Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Officials argued that as an adopted heir he should lessen mourning for his natural mother; blaming the princely household staff, they impeached minister Zhuge Yi.

sentences.zh: 王上疏曰：「亡母生臨臣國，沒留國第，臣雖出後，亦無所厭，則私情得敘。

translations.literal: The prince presented a memorial stating: “My late mother in life faced my march; in death she remains at the march residence; although I have gone out as heir to another, there is nothing I resent—then private feeling obtains its expression.
translations.idiomatic: He replied: “My mother lived and died within my princedom; though I was posthumously adopted out, I still owe her full grief.”

sentences.zh: 昔敬后崩，孝王已出繼，亦還服重。

translations.literal: Formerly when Empress Jing died, Prince Xiao had already gone out in succession, yet he still returned to wear heavy mourning.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Jing passed away, Prince Xiao had likewise been adopted elsewhere, yet he still came back to mourn her fully.

sentences.zh: 此則明比，臣所憲章也。

translations.literal: This is a clear parallel; it is what I take as my model.
translations.idiomatic: That precedent is plain, and it is the rule I follow.

sentences.zh: 」明穆皇后不奪其志，乃徙琅邪王為會稽王，追號后曰會稽太妃。

translations.literal: ” Empress Mingmu did not override his intent; thereupon the Prince of Langya was moved to be Prince of Kuaiji, and she was posthumously titled Grand Consort of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Yu the Solemn accepted his plea: Sima Yu became Prince of Kuaiji, and Lady Zheng was honored posthumously as Grand Consort of Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 及簡文帝即位，未及追尊。

translations.literal: When Emperor Jianwen ascended, there was not yet time to posthumously exalt her.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jianwen had no chance to elevate her title before other business crowded in.

sentences.zh: 臨崩，封皇子道子為琅邪王，領會稽國，奉太妃祀。

translations.literal: On the verge of death, he enfeoffed imperial son Daozi as Prince of Langya, heading the Kuaiji march, to perform sacrifice to the grand consort.
translations.idiomatic: Dying, he made Sima Daozi Prince of Langya with Kuaiji income to maintain her shrine.

sentences.zh: 太元十九年，孝武帝下詔曰：「會稽太妃文母之德，徽音有融，誕載聖明，光延于晉。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year of Taiyuan, Emperor Xiaowu issued an edict stating: “The Grand Consort of Kuaiji had the virtue of King Wen’s mother; her fine repute shone bright; she bore and raised the sage and bright one, extending glory to Jin.
translations.idiomatic: In 394 Emperor Xiaowu proclaimed Lady Zheng’s motherly virtue and her role in rearing Jianwen.

sentences.zh: 先帝追尊聖善，朝議不一，道以疑屈。

translations.literal: The late Emperor pursued exalting her sagely goodness; court deliberation was not unified, and the Way was left in doubtful abasement.
translations.idiomatic: Jianwen had tried to honor her, but ministers disagreed and the matter stalled.

sentences.zh: 朕述遵先志，常惕于心。

translations.literal: I narrate and follow former intent, constantly fearful at heart.
translations.idiomatic: I mean to finish what he began and have long felt uneasy about the delay.

sentences.zh: 今仰奉遺旨，依陽秋二漢孝懷皇帝故事，上太妃尊號曰簡文太后。

translations.literal: Now, looking up I obey the testamentary intent; following the Spring and Autumn annals and the two Han precedents for Emperor Xiaohuai, I raise the grand consort’s honored title to Dowager Empress Jianwen.
translations.idiomatic: He cited Han and chronicle precedent and raised her to Dowager Empress Jianwen.

sentences.zh: 」[8]于是立廟于太廟路西，陵曰嘉平。

translations.literal: ” [Note 8] Thereupon a temple was erected west of the Grand Temple road; the mausoleum was called Jiaping.
translations.idiomatic: A shrine went up west of the imperial temple; she was buried at Jiaping Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 時群臣希旨，多謂鄭太后應配食于元帝者。

translations.literal: At that time the host of ministers, hoping to hit the ruler’s wish, mostly said Dowager Empress Zheng ought to receive joint offerings with Emperor Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Flatterers urged that she share Emperor Yuan’s altar in the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 帝以問太子前率徐邈，邈曰：「臣案陽秋之義，母以子貴。

translations.literal: The Emperor asked former forward leader of the crown prince’s guard Xu Miao; Miao said: “I examine the Spring and Autumn meaning: the mother is honored through the son.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Miao told him the classic rule: a woman’s rank rises with her son.

sentences.zh: 魯隱尊桓母，別考仲子之宮而不配食于惠廟。

translations.literal: Duke Yin of Lu honored Huan’s mother, separately enshrining Zhongzi’s chamber and not joining offerings in Hui’s temple.
translations.idiomatic: Lu’s Duke Yin built a side shrine for Lady Zhongzi instead of seating her beside Duke Hui.

sentences.zh: 又平素之時，不伉儷于先帝，至于子孫，豈可為祖考立配？

translations.literal: Moreover in ordinary times she was not paired as spouse to the late Emperor; extending to descendants, how can one for ancestors and grandfathers establish a mate?
translations.idiomatic: Lady Zheng had never been Yuan’s principal wife; she could not be retrofitted as his temple consort.

sentences.zh: 其崇尊盡禮，由於臣子，故得稱太后，陵廟備典。

translations.literal: Her exalted honor and full rites come from the ministers and sons; therefore she could be called dowager empress, and mausoleum and temple match the canon.
translations.idiomatic: Her titles and tomb were gifts of a grateful son, which is why she could be called dowager at all.

sentences.zh: 若乃祔葬配食，則義所不可。

translations.literal: As for joint burial and joint offerings, that is what the meaning forbids.
translations.idiomatic: Joint burial beside Yuan, however, was ritually improper.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: ” They followed it.
translations.idiomatic: The throne accepted his reasoning.

sentences.zh: 簡文順王皇后

translations.literal: Empress Wang, posthumous epithets Jianwen and Shun.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wang the Complaisant (Jianwen and Shun)

sentences.zh: 孝武文李太后

translations.literal: Dowager Empress Li, posthumous epithets Xiaowu and Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Dowager Li of Xiaowu and the Cultured

sentences.zh: 孝武文李太后諱陵容，本出微賤。

translations.literal: The Xiaowu-Wen Dowager Li’s taboo name was Lingrong; originally she came from humble status.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Li Lingrong, mother of Emperor Xiaowu, began life in the lowest palace ranks.

sentences.zh: 始簡文帝為會稽王，有三子，俱夭。

translations.literal: At first, when Emperor Jianwen was Prince of Kuaiji, he had three sons; all died young.
translations.idiomatic: As Prince of Kuaiji he had three boys, none of whom survived.

sentences.zh: 自道生廢黜，獻王早世，其後諸姬絕孕將十年。

translations.literal: From Daosheng’s deposition and removal, and Prince Xian’s early death, thereafter the various ladies had no pregnancy for nearly ten years.
translations.idiomatic: After one heir was cast aside and another prince died in youth, his concubines bore no children for almost a decade.

sentences.zh: 帝令卜者扈謙筮之，曰：「後房中有一女，當育二貴男，其一終盛晉室。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered diviner Hu Qian to cast yarrow stalks; he said: “In the rear chambers there is one woman who will bear two noble sons; one of them will ultimately bring great prosperity to the house of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Qian divined that a palace woman would bear two sons, one destined to revive the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 」時徐貴人生新安公主，以德美見寵。

translations.literal: ” At that time Honored Person Xu bore the Princess of Xin’an and by virtue and beauty enjoyed favor.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Xu had already given him the Princess of Xin’an and was his favorite.

sentences.zh: 帝常冀之有娠，而彌年無子。

translations.literal: The Emperor constantly hoped she would be pregnant, yet a full year brought no son.
translations.idiomatic: He longed for a child from her, but year after year she conceived nothing.

sentences.zh: 會有道士許邁者，朝臣時望多稱其得道。

translations.literal: There was a Daoist, Xu Mai, whom courtiers of the time mostly praised as having attained the Way.
translations.idiomatic: The Daoist Xu Mai was widely rumored to possess transcendental arts.

sentences.zh: 帝從容問焉，答曰：「邁是好山水人，本無道術，斯事豈所能判！

translations.literal: The Emperor casually asked him; he answered: “Mai is a man who loves mountains and rivers; fundamentally he has no Daoist arts—how could he judge such matters!
translations.idiomatic: Xu Mai admitted he was no thaumaturge.

sentences.zh: 但殿下德厚慶深，宜隆奕世之緒，當從扈謙之言，以存廣接之道。

translations.literal: Only Your Highness’s virtue is thick and blessing deep; you ought to enlarge a lineage lasting many generations—you should follow Hu Qian’s words and keep open the way of broad reception.
translations.idiomatic: He urged the prince to trust Hu Qian’s advice and cast his net wider among the women.

sentences.zh: 」帝然之，更加採納。

translations.literal: ” The Emperor approved it and further expanded selection.
translations.idiomatic: Jianwen agreed and broadened the search.

sentences.zh: 又數年無子，乃令善相者召諸愛妾而示之，皆云非其人，又悉以諸婢媵示焉。

translations.literal: Again several years passed with no sons; then he ordered a skilled physiognomist to summon his beloved concubines and show them—all said they were not the person; then he showed all the maidservants and attendants as well.
translations.idiomatic: Years later, still childless, he lined up every favorite and then every maid for a face-reader; none fit the omen until the very last ranks.

sentences.zh: 時后為宮人，在織坊中，形長而色黑，宮人皆謂之崑崙。

translations.literal: At that time the empress was a palace woman in the weaving workshop, tall in frame and dark in complexion; the palace women all called her Kunlun.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Li worked in the textile ward—tall and dark-skinned, the others nicknamed her “Kunlun.”

sentences.zh: 既至，相者驚云：「此其人也。

translations.literal: When she arrived, the physiognomist startled and said: “This is the one.
translations.idiomatic: The reader took one look and cried, “Here she is.”

sentences.zh: 」帝以大計，召之侍寢。

translations.literal: ” The Emperor, for the great plan, summoned her to attend the bedchamber.
translations.idiomatic: For the sake of the succession he called her to his couch.

sentences.zh: 后數夢兩龍枕膝，日月入懷，意以為吉祥，向儕類說之，帝聞而異焉，遂生孝武帝及會稽文孝王、鄱陽長公主。

translations.literal: The empress repeatedly dreamed two dragons pillowed on her knees, sun and moon entering her bosom; she thought it auspicious and told her companions; the Emperor heard and marveled—thereupon she bore Emperor Xiaowu, Prince Wenxiao of Kuaiji, and the Princess of Poyang.
translations.idiomatic: She dreamed of dragons cradling her knees and heavenly bodies in her womb; when she told the others, Jianwen listened—and she bore Xiaowu, Sima Daozi, and the long princess of Poyang.

sentences.zh: 及孝武帝初即位，尊為淑妃。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu first ascended, she was honored as Shufei.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaowu first titled her Honored Consort Shufei.

sentences.zh: 太元三年，進為貴人。

translations.literal: In the third year of Taiyuan she was advanced to Honored Person.
translations.idiomatic: In 378 she became an Honored Person.

sentences.zh: 九年，又進為夫人。

translations.literal: In the ninth year she was again advanced to Lady.
translations.idiomatic: By 384 she was raised to Lady.

sentences.zh: 十二年，加為皇太妃，儀服一同太后。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year she was further titled imperial grand consort; ritual garb was identical to an empress dowager’s.
translations.idiomatic: In 387 she became imperial grand consort with a dowager’s regalia.

sentences.zh: 十九年，會稽王道子啟：「母以子貴，慶厚禮崇。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year, Prince of Kuaiji Daozi stated: “The mother is honored through the son; blessing is thick and rites exalted.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Daozi argued that her son’s throne justified greater honor.

sentences.zh: 伏惟皇太妃純德光大，休祐攸鍾，啟嘉祚於聖明，嗣徽音于上列。

translations.literal: We humbly consider that the imperial grand consort’s pure virtue shines broadly; auspicious protection concentrates on her; she opened blessed fortune in the sage and bright, continuing fine repute in the highest ranks.
translations.idiomatic: He praised her virtue and her role in producing the sage-king.

sentences.zh: 雖幽顯同謀，而稱謂未盡，非所以仰述聖心，允答天人。

translations.literal: Although hidden and manifest together plotted, the title is not yet complete—this is not how to narrate upward the sage heart or faithfully answer Heaven and man.
translations.idiomatic: Her titles still fell short of what Heaven and humanity expected.

sentences.zh: 宜崇正名號，詳案舊典。

translations.literal: It is fitting to exalt the correct name and title, examining in detail the old canons.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that canonical titles be settled once and for all.

sentences.zh: 」八月辛巳，帝臨軒，遣兼太保劉耽尊為皇太后，稱崇訓宮。

translations.literal: ” On xinsi day of the eighth month the Emperor faced the gallery and dispatched concurrent Grand Guardian Liu Dan to honor her as empress dowager, titled Chongxun Palace.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn Xiaowu received ministers in state and sent Liu Dan to invest her as Dowager of Chongxun Palace.

sentences.zh: 安帝即位，尊為太皇太后。

translations.literal: When Emperor An ascended, she was honored as grand empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor An elevated her to grand dowager.

sentences.zh: 隆安四年，崩于含章殿。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Longan she died in Hanzhang Hall.
translations.idiomatic: She died in 400 in Hanzhang Hall.

sentences.zh: 朝議疑其服制，左僕射何澄、右僕射王雅、尚書車胤、孔安國[9]、祠部郎徐廣等議曰：「太皇太后名位允正，體同皇極，理制備盡，情禮兼申。

translations.literal: Court deliberation doubted her mourning garments; Left Vice Director He Cheng, Right Vice Director Wang Ya, Director Che Yin, Kong Anguo [note 9], Xu Guang of the Sacrifices Bureau and others argued: “The grand empress dowager’s name and position are rightly ordered; her person matches the supreme pole; principle and regulation are fully provided; feeling and rite both extend.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers debated mourning for her: He Cheng, Wang Ya, Che Yin, Kong Anguo, and Xu Guang cited precedent.

sentences.zh: 陽秋之義，母以子貴，既稱夫人，禮服從正。

translations.literal: By Spring and Autumn meaning, the mother is honored through the son; having been titled Lady, ritual garments follow the principal.
translations.idiomatic: Once styled Lady, her son owed her the full mourning of a mother.

sentences.zh: 故成風顯夫人之號，文公服三年之喪。

translations.literal: Therefore Chengfeng bore the manifest title of Lady, and Duke Wen of Lu wore three years’ mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Wen of Lu mourned Lady Chengfeng for three years.

sentences.zh: 子于父母之所生，體尊義重。

translations.literal: A son toward the parents who bore him—embodiment is exalted and duty weighty.
translations.idiomatic: A child’s debt to the parent who gave life is absolute.

sentences.zh: 且禮祖不厭孫，固宜追服無屈，而緣情立制。

translations.literal: Moreover in rite the grandfather does not displace the grandson; solidly it is fitting to pursue mourning without bending, and by following feeling establish regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Ancestors do not cancel a grandson’s debt to a grandmother; feeling must shape the rule.

sentences.zh: 若嫌明文不存，則疑斯從重，謂應同于為祖母後齊衰三年。

translations.literal: If one worries explicit text does not survive, then in doubt follow the heavy side—we hold it should match wearing hemmed sackcloth three years as heir after a grandmother.
translations.idiomatic: Where texts were silent, they chose the heavier obligation: three years’ hemmed sackcloth as for a grandmother.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: ” They followed it.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 皇后及百官皆服齊衰期，永安皇后一舉哀。

translations.literal: The empress and the hundred officials all wore hemmed sackcloth for the one-year period; the Yong’an Empress performed one bout of wailing.
translations.idiomatic: Empress and officials observed one year’s hemmed mourning; the Yong’an empress led a single public lament.

sentences.zh: 於是設廬於西堂，凶儀施于神獸門，葬修平陵，神主祔于宣太后廟。

translations.literal: Thereupon a hut was set up in the west hall; mourning gear was deployed at Divine Beast Gate; burial was at Xiuping Mausoleum; the spirit tablet was joined in Empress Dowager Xuan’s temple.
translations.idiomatic: A mourning lodge rose in the west hall; the catafalque passed Divine Beast Gate; she was buried at Xiuping and enshrined beside Empress Dowager Xuan.

sentences.zh: 孝武定王皇后

translations.literal: Empress Wang, posthumous epithets Xiaowu and Ding.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wang the Settled (Xiaowu and Ding)

sentences.zh: 孝武定王皇后諱法慧，哀靖皇后之姪也。

translations.literal: The Xiaowu-Ding Empress Wang’s taboo name was Fahui; she was a niece of Empress Ai-Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wang Fahui was a niece of Empress Wang the Lamented.

sentences.zh: 父蘊，見《外戚傳》。

translations.literal: Her father was Yun; see the “Biographies of the Consort Families.”
translations.idiomatic: Her father Wang Yun appears among the consort kin.

sentences.zh: 初，帝將納后，訪于公卿。

translations.literal: At first, when the Emperor was about to take an empress, he consulted dukes and ministers.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaowu sought a bride, he polled his ministers.

sentences.zh: 于時蘊子恭以弱冠見僕射謝安，安深敬重之。

translations.literal: At that time Yun’s son Gong, at capping age, met Vice Director Xie An; An deeply respected him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yun’s son Wang Gong, barely twenty, impressed Xie An.

sentences.zh: 既而謂人曰：「昔毛嘉恥于魏朝，楊駿幾傾晉室。

translations.literal: Afterward he told others: “Formerly Mao Jia was shamed in the Wei court; Yang Jun nearly overturned the house of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Xie later warned that lowborn in-laws had nearly ruined Wei and Western Jin.

sentences.zh: 若帝納后，有父者，唯廕望如王蘊乃可。

translations.literal: If the Emperor takes an empress who has a living father, only one with pedigree and repute like Wang Yun will do.
translations.idiomatic: Only a father as reputable as Wang Yun would suit the throne.

sentences.zh: 」既而訪蘊女，容德淑令，乃舉以應選。
