translations.literal: ” Thereupon he inquired after Yun’s daughter; her looks and virtue were chaste and fine—thereupon she was recommended to answer selection.
translations.idiomatic: They proposed Wang Yun’s daughter, noted for beauty and conduct.

sentences.zh: 寧康三年，中軍將軍桓沖等奏曰：「臣聞天地之道，蓋相須而化成；

translations.literal: In the third year of Ningkang, Central Army general Huan Chong and others memorialized: “We have heard that the way of Heaven and Earth relies on mutual need to complete transformation;
translations.idiomatic: In 375 Huan Chong led a memorial on the cosmic harmony of sovereign and consort.

sentences.zh: 帝后之德，必相協而政隆。

translations.literal: The virtue of emperor and empress must harmonize each other for government to flourish.
translations.idiomatic: Sovereign and consort must complement one another.

sentences.zh: 然後品物流形，彝倫攸敘，靈根長固，本枝百世。

translations.literal: Only then do the myriad kinds flow into form, constant human relations find order, the numinous root stands long firm, and root and branches last a hundred generations.
translations.idiomatic: Then the dynasty’s bloodline stays secure for generations.

sentences.zh: 天人同致，莫不由此。

translations.literal: Heaven and man reach the same goal—none do not proceed from this.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven and humanity alike depend on that harmony.

sentences.zh: 是以塗山作儷，而夏族以熙；

translations.literal: Therefore Tushan became mate and the Xia house flourished;
translations.idiomatic: Tushan wed Yu and Xia rose;

sentences.zh: 妊姒配周，而姬祚以昌。

translations.literal: Si of Zhou was paired with Zhou and the Ji fortune grew glorious.
translations.idiomatic: the Jiang women matched the Zhou kings and the Ji clan prospered.

sentences.zh: 今長秋將建，宜時簡擇。

translations.literal: Now Changqiu is about to be established; it is time to select promptly.
translations.idiomatic: The empress’s seat stood empty and needed filling.

sentences.zh: 伏聞試守晉陵太守王蘊女，天性柔順，四業允備。

translations.literal: We have heard that Acting Governor of Jinling Wang Yun’s daughter is by nature gentle and compliant, the four womanly arts fully provided.
translations.idiomatic: They recommended Wang Yun’s daughter, acting governor of Jinling, as versed in every womanly art.

sentences.zh: 且盛德之冑，美善先積。

translations.literal: Moreover she is of a house of abundant virtue; goodness has long accumulated.
translations.idiomatic: Her clan’s virtue was beyond question.

sentences.zh: 臣等參議，可以配德乾元，恭承宗廟，徽音六宮，母儀天下。

translations.literal: We ministers jointly deliberate: she can match virtue with Qian’s origin, reverently sustain the ancestral temple, extend fine repute through the six palaces, and be mother-model to All Under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: They declared her fit to be empress and mother of the realm.

sentences.zh: 」於是帝始納焉。

translations.literal: ” Thereupon the Emperor first took her in.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaowu accepted their choice.

sentences.zh: 封蘊妻劉氏為樂平鄉君。

translations.literal: Yun’s wife Lady Liu was enfeoffed Mistress of Leping township.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Liu, Wang Yun’s wife, became Mistress of Leping township.

sentences.zh: 后性嗜酒驕妒，帝深患之。

translations.literal: The empress by nature loved wine, was arrogant and jealous; the Emperor deeply suffered from it.
translations.idiomatic: She drank heavily and flew into jealous rages; Xiaowu found her exhausting.

sentences.zh: 乃召蘊於東堂，具說后過狀，令加訓誡。

translations.literal: Thereupon he summoned Yun to the Eastern Hall, fully stating the empress’s faults, ordering him to add instruction and warning.
translations.idiomatic: He called Wang Yun to the Eastern Hall and listed her misdeeds, demanding parental correction.

sentences.zh: 蘊免冠謝焉。

translations.literal: Yun removed cap and apologized.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yun doffed his cap and begged forgiveness.

sentences.zh: 后於是少自改飾。

translations.literal: The empress thereupon somewhat reformed and adorned herself.
translations.idiomatic: The empress mended her ways, if only a little.

sentences.zh: 太元五年崩，年二十一，葬隆平陵。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Taiyuan she died; she was twenty-one sui and was buried at Longping Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: She died in 380 at twenty-one and was buried at Longping Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 安德陳太后

translations.literal: Dowager Empress Chen, posthumous epithet Ande.
translations.idiomatic: Dowager Chen the Peaceful and Virtuous

sentences.zh: 安僖王皇后

translations.literal: Empress Wang, posthumous epithets An and Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wang the Secure and Diligent

sentences.zh: 安僖王皇后諱神愛，琅邪臨沂人也。

translations.literal: The An-Xi Empress Wang’s taboo name was Shen’ai; she was a native of Linyi in Langya commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wang Shen’ai came from the Langya Wang clan in Linyi.

sentences.zh: 父獻之，見別傳；

translations.literal: Her father was Xianzhi; see his separate biography;
translations.idiomatic: Her father was Wang Xianzhi, whose life is told elsewhere;

sentences.zh: 母新安愍公主。

translations.literal: her mother was Princess Xin’an Min.
translations.idiomatic: her mother the Princess of Xin’an, posthumous epithet Min.

sentences.zh: 后以太元二十一年納為太子妃。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year of Taiyuan she was taken in as crown princess.
translations.idiomatic: In 396 she became crown princess.

sentences.zh: 及安帝即位，立為皇后。

translations.literal: When Emperor An ascended, she was established as empress.
translations.idiomatic: When An took the throne, she became empress.

sentences.zh: 無子。

translations.literal: She had no sons.
translations.idiomatic: She bore no children.

sentences.zh: 義熙八年崩于徽音殿，時年二十九，葬休平陵。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Yixi she died in Huiyin Hall; at the time she was twenty-nine sui and was buried at Xiuping Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: She died in 412 in Huiyin Hall at twenty-nine and was buried at Xiuping Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 恭思褚皇后

translations.literal: Empress Chu, posthumous epithets Gong and Si.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Chu the Reverent and Thoughtful

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：方祇體安，儷乾儀而合德；

translations.literal: The historian says: The square earth deity embodies tranquility; paired with Heaven’s pattern, they unite in virtue.
translations.idiomatic: The annalist writes: earth rests square and mates with heaven’s design, sharing one virtue.

sentences.zh: 圓舒循晷，配羲曜以齊明。

translations.literal: The round moon follows the sundial’s shadow; matched with the sun’s brilliance, they shine as one.
translations.idiomatic: Moon and sun trace each other’s course and light the cosmos together.

sentences.zh: 故知陽爍陰凝，萬物假其陶鑄；

translations.literal: Thus we know yang’s radiance and yin’s stillness—all things receive their casting from them;
translations.idiomatic: From yang’s fire and yin’s deep all things take shape;

sentences.zh: 火炎水潤，六氣由其調理。

translations.literal: fire flames and water moistens; the six qi are ordered through them.
translations.idiomatic: as flame and flood temper the six seasonal breaths.

sentences.zh: 取譬賢淑，作伉文思，靈根式固，實資於此。

translations.literal: Taking likeness from worthy and chaste consorts, they become partners in pattern and reflection; the numinous root stands firm—truly this is what supplies it.
translations.idiomatic: Wise wives mirror heaven’s pairing; the dynasty’s taproot holds fast because of them.

sentences.zh: 宣穆閱禮，偶德潛鱗，翊天造之艱虞，嗣塗山之逸響，寶運歸其後胤，蓋有母儀之助焉。

translations.literal: Consort Xuanmu mastered ritual, coupled in virtue while still hidden as a fish; she aided the hardships of Heaven’s forging and echoed Tushan’s distant renown; the precious Mandate returned to her descendants—surely there was the assistance of a mother-model therein.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang the August and Solemn walked in rites beside a rising dragon, endured the founding’s perils, and left a line that inherited the throne—such is the power of true motherhood.

sentences.zh: 武元楊氏預聞朝政，明不逮遠，愛溺私情，深杜衛瓘之言，不曉張泓之詐，運其陰沴，韜映乾明，晉道中微，基于是矣。

translations.literal: Lady Yang of Wu Yuan foreknew court government; her clarity did not reach far; doting on private feeling, she deeply blocked Wei Guan’s words and did not perceive Zhang Hong’s deceit; she wielded her yin balefulness, veiling and dimming Qian’s brightness—the Jin path declined in the middle; the foundation lay herein.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Yang meddled in Emperor Wu’s court: blinded by favor, she silenced Wei Guan and missed Zhang Hong’s plot, letting dark intrigue eclipse the throne—the mid-Jin slump began with her.

sentences.zh: 惠皇稟質，王縱其嚚，識暗鳴蛙，智昏文蛤。

translations.literal: Emperor Hui received his substance; the empress indulged his stubborn folly; his discernment was dark as croaking frogs, his wit muddled as patterned clams.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Hui was a weak vessel; Empress Jia stoked his cruelty until he could neither see nor think straight.

sentences.zh: 南風肆狡，扇禍稽天。

translations.literal: Nanfeng wantonly wielded cunning, fanning calamity to the heavens.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Nanfeng’s malice fanned disaster across the realm.

sentences.zh: 初踐椒宮，逞梟心于長樂；

translations.literal: First treading the pepper palace, she displayed an owl heart in Changle;
translations.idiomatic: From the harem she nursed a predator’s heart and struck first at Changle Palace;

sentences.zh: 方觀梓樹，頒鴆羽於離明。

translations.literal: then viewing the catalpa tree, she dispensed aconite feathers in the southern radiance.
translations.idiomatic: then, beside the heir’s courtyard, she dealt poison in broad daylight.

sentences.zh: 褒后滅周，方之蓋小；

translations.literal: Baosi destroyed Zhou—set beside her, that seems small;
translations.idiomatic: Baosi’s ruin of Zhou pales beside this;

sentences.zh: 妹妃傾夏，曾何足喻。

translations.literal: Moxi overturned Xia—how could it suffice for analogy?
translations.idiomatic: Moxi’s toppling of Xia is hardly a closer match.

sentences.zh: 中原陷於鳴鏑，其兆彰於此焉。

translations.literal: The Central Plain sank beneath whistling arrows; its omen shone forth here.
translations.idiomatic: The heartland’s fall to steppe armies was foreshadowed in these palace crimes.

sentences.zh: 昔者高宗諒闇，總百官於元老；

translations.literal: Of old Gaozong in the mourning hut gathered the hundred offices under elder ministers;
translations.idiomatic: High Shang’s king mourned in silence while veterans ran the ministries;

sentences.zh: 成王沖眇，託萬機於上公。

translations.literal: King Cheng was young and tiny; he entrusted the myriad threads to the senior duke.
translations.idiomatic: the boy King Cheng gave every thread of policy to the Duke of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 太后御宸，諒知非古。

translations.literal: An empress dowager grasping the imperial seat—we may trust this was not antiquity’s way.
translations.idiomatic: Women on the throne was never classical practice—yet it happened.

sentences.zh: 而明穆、康獻，仍世臨朝，時屬委裘，躬行負扆。

translations.literal: Yet Mingmu and Kang-Xian, reign after reign faced the court; the times called for handing the robe; they personally bore the screen behind the ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Still Empresses Yu and Chu ruled in succession when the boy emperors could not, each holding the regency in person.

sentences.zh: 各免華陽之釁，竟躡和熹之蹤，保陵遲以克終，所幸實為多矣。

translations.literal: Each avoided Huayang’s strife, yet trod in He Xi’s footprints, preserving decline until a decent close—the good fortune was already much.
translations.idiomatic: They skirted the worst coups, followed Han’s able dowagers, and brought unstable times to a peaceful end—no small mercy.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：二妃光舜，三母翼周。

translations.literal: The eulogy says: The two consorts shone on Shun; the three mothers winged Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: The verdict runs: Shun’s wives brought light; Zhou’s three mothers lifted the throne.

sentences.zh: 末升夷癸，褒進亡幽。

translations.literal: Mo Xi and the debauched Gui rose late; Baosi advanced and You perished in obscurity.
translations.idiomatic: The last evils of Xia’s court met Shang’s ruin; Baosi’s favor buried You in darkness.

sentences.zh: 家邦興滅，職此之由。

translations.literal: House and state’s rise and fall—duty lies herein.
translations.idiomatic: Dynasties rise or fall on choices such as these.

sentences.zh: 穆后沈斷，忘情執爨。

translations.literal: Empress Mu was deep and decisive; forgetting feeling, she took the kitchen ladle.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Yu Wenjun was resolute: she set private ties aside and kept to humble duty.

sentences.zh: 故劍辭恩，池蒲起歎。

translations.literal: The old sword declined favor; pool reeds raised a sigh.
translations.idiomatic: She remembered the “old sword” and spurned new favorites—hence the poem’s lament.

sentences.zh: 崇化繁祉，肇基商亂。

translations.literal: Exalting transformation, multiplying blessing—yet the foundation opened Shang’s turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: Her virtue brought blessings, yet it also laid the tinder for later chaos.

sentences.zh: 二楊繼寵，福極災生。

translations.literal: The two Yangs succeeded in favor; blessing reached its peak and disaster was born.
translations.idiomatic: Two Yang consorts rose in turn; fortune peaked—and calamity followed.

sentences.zh: 南風熾虐，國喪身傾。

translations.literal: Nanfeng burned fierce and cruel; the state perished and her person overturned.
translations.idiomatic: Nanfeng’s tyranny broke the realm and destroyed herself.

sentences.zh: 獻容幸亂，居辱疑榮。

translations.literal: Xianrong rode chaos, dwelling in shame yet seeming glorious.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xianrong traded on turmoil, mistaking humiliation for honor.

sentences.zh: 援筆廢主，持尺威帝。

translations.literal: Wielding brush to depose the lord, holding foot-rule to awe the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: She drafted edicts to unthrone emperors and brandished regalia to cow the throne.

sentences.zh: 契闊終罹，殷憂以斃。

translations.literal: Partings and hardships ended in disaster; deep grief killed her.
translations.idiomatic: Separation and sorrow finished her; anxiety at last took her life.

sentences.zh: 芬實窈窕，芳菲婉嫕。

translations.literal: Fen was truly graceful and slender, fragrant and softly fair.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Zuo Fen—slender grace, gentle perfume.

sentences.zh: 呂妾變嬴，黃姬化羋。

translations.literal: The Lü concubine changed the Ying line; the yellow consort turned to Mi.
translations.idiomatic: Like Lü Zhi swapping the imperial surname or the Mi women shifting Chu’s bloodline, blood and throne mixed.

sentences.zh: 石文遠著，金行潛徙。

translations.literal: Stone inscriptions showed from afar; the metal phase quietly shifted.
translations.idiomatic: Portents were carved in stone while the Jin “metal” Mandate silently slipped away.

sentences.zh: 婦德傾城，迷朱奪紫。

translations.literal: Wifely virtue could overturn a wall; vermillion was lost and purple usurped.
translations.idiomatic: A woman’s wiles could shake a capital, swapping rightful rank for usurped purple.

sentences.zh: 校勘記

translations.literal: Collation notes.
translations.idiomatic: Textual notes

sentences.zh: 「安陵縣君」斠注：《御覽·二〇二》引《中興書》「安陵」作「安陽」。

translations.literal: On “Mistress of Anling county”: the Imperial Digest, fascicle 202, citing the Zhongxing shu, writes “Anling” as “Anyang.”
translations.idiomatic: A collation note: the Zhongxing shu reads “Anyang” instead of “Anling.”

sentences.zh: 按：晉無安陵縣，而有東安陵縣，疑此當作「安陽縣君」。

translations.literal: Comment: Jin had no Anling county, but did have Eastern Anling county; suspect this should read “Mistress of Anyang county.”
translations.idiomatic: Jin geography had no Anling; editors suspect “Anyang” was intended.

sentences.zh: 「諱陵陽」考異：《宋書·州郡志》杜皇后諱陵，此衍「陽」字。

translations.literal: On “taboo name Lingyang”: textual comparison—the Songshu “Treatise on Provinces and Commanderies” gives Empress Du’s taboo as Ling only; this text mistakenly adds “yang.”
translations.idiomatic: The Song history records her name as Ling, not Lingyang; “yang” is likely a scribal addition.

sentences.zh: 咸康四年以後諱改宣城之陵陽縣為廣陽，可證后名無「陽」字。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Xiankang the name taboo led to renaming Lingyang county in Xuancheng to Guangyang, confirming her name lacked “yang.”
translations.idiomatic: The 338 renaming of Lingyang county proves the extra character is wrong.

sentences.zh: 「及哀帝、海西公之世，太后復臨朝稱制」李校：《哀帝紀》惟興寧二年帝以服藥致疾，崇德太后復臨朝攝政，至《海西公紀》不言有臨朝事，「世」字當是「際」字之誤。

translations.literal: On “in the eras of Emperor Ai and the Prince of Haixi, the empress dowager again faced the court”: Li’s note—the Annals of Emperor Ai record only that in the second year of Xingning, after the emperor fell ill from drugs, Chongde Empress Dowager resumed facing the court as regent; the Annals of the Prince of Haixi do not mention her holding court; the character “era” is probably an error for “juncture.”
translations.idiomatic: Editorial note: only Emperor Ai’s reign shows a return to regency; the word translated as eras should probably read at the juncture (between the two reigns).

sentences.zh: 「以明尊卑」：《禮志·中》、《宋志·二》、《通典·八〇》、《通考·一二一》「尊卑」皆作「尊尊」，乃用穀梁傳文公二年「君子不以親親害尊尊」之義。

translations.literal: On “to clarify high and low”: the Rites Treatise (middle), Song Treatise 2, Tongdian 80, and Tongkao 121 all write “zunzun” (honoring rank) rather than “zunbei,” following the Guliang reading for Duke Wen’s second year: “the noble man does not let kinship harm honoring rank.”
translations.idiomatic: Variant: other sources read zunzun (priority of public rank) per the Guliang commentary.

sentences.zh: 徐藻、徐邈父子治穀梁，此作「尊尊」為是。

translations.literal: Xu Zao and his son Xu Miao studied the Guliang; writing “zunzun” here is correct.
translations.idiomatic: Because the Xu family specialized in Guliang, the zunzun reading is preferred.

sentences.zh: 元興三年崩：「元興」原作「永興」。

translations.literal: “Died in the third year of Yuanxing”: the original text wrote “Yongxing.”
translations.idiomatic: Colophon: the era name was miswritten as Yongxing instead of Yuanxing.

sentences.zh: 商榷：「永興」當作「元興」，自穆帝升平元年至安帝元興三年，正四十八年。

translations.literal: Discussion: “Yongxing” should be “Yuanxing”; from Emperor Mu’s first year of Shengping to Emperor An’s third year of Yuanxing is exactly forty-eight years.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars note forty-eight years on the throne matches Yuanxing 3, not Yongxing.

sentences.zh: 按：《安紀》、《建康實錄·一〇》皆在元興三年，今據改。

translations.literal: Comment: the Annals of Emperor An and Jiankang shilu 10 both place the event in Yuanxing 3; the text is emended accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Standard histories agree on Yuanxing 3; the edition adopts that date.

sentences.zh: 「太元十一年海西公薨」：「十一年」原作「九年」。

translations.literal: On “the Prince of Haixi died in the eleventh year of Taiyuan”: the original read “ninth year.”
translations.idiomatic: Colophon: Taiyuan 11 was misprinted as Taiyuan 9.

sentences.zh: 《海西公紀》、《孝武紀》、《建康實錄·九》、《六朝事跡類編》俱作「太元十一年」，今據改。

translations.literal: The Annals of the Prince of Haixi, Annals of Emperor Xiaowu, Jiankang shilu 9, and Liuchao shiji leibian all read “eleventh year of Taiyuan”; emended accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Parallel sources unanimously give Taiyuan 11.

sentences.zh: 「簡文太后」斠注：當從《孝武紀》作「簡文宣太后」。

translations.literal: On “Dowager Empress Jianwen”: collation note—it should follow the Annals of Emperor Xiaowu as “Dowager Empress Jianwen and Xuan.”
translations.idiomatic: Title should include “Xuan” as in the Xiaowu annals.

sentences.zh: 按：《冊府·二九》亦有「宣」字。

translations.literal: Comment: Cefu yuangui 29 also contains the character “Xuan.”
translations.idiomatic: The Cefu yuangui preserves the “Xuan” character as well.

sentences.zh: 「孔安國」：據《孔安國傳》，安國時為領軍，「孔安國」上疑脫「領軍」二字。

translations.literal: On “Kong Anguo”: according to Kong Anguo’s biography, at the time he was commanding the guards; above “Kong Anguo” the two characters “commanding the guards” are probably missing.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Anguo’s entry suggests the title Commander of the Guards probably dropped out before his name.
